sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Accessibility = **semantic HTML first**, ARIA second.

- **Landmarks** — `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<aside>`, `<footer>`.
- **Forms** — `<label>` + `<input>` association; `aria-describedby` for errors.
- **Keyboard** — Tab order matches visual order; never trap focus.
- **Screen readers** — test with NVDA / VoiceOver before shipping.
- **WCAG 2.1 AA** is the legal floor in many jurisdictions.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
The interview surface for this module breaks into these focus areas:

- **Html5 semantic elements** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Forms and inputs** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Aria roles and attributes** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Wcag and accessibility** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Keyboard navigation** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Screen readers** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Scenario-based** — applied questions tying multiple topics together. Drill these *last*, after the fundamentals are sharp.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Use `<button>`, not `<div onClick>`** — saves 90% of accessibility bugs.
- **Skip links** — `Skip to content` anchor for keyboard users.
- **Focus management** in SPAs — set focus on route change.
- **Colour contrast** — 4.5:1 for normal text; check with Lighthouse.
- **`aria-live`** for dynamic content updates (toasts, errors).

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'd reach for the semantic element first, layer ARIA only when semantics aren't enough, test keyboard navigation manually, run axe-core in CI, and verify with a screen reader before shipping. WCAG 2.1 AA is my baseline."*
